items.title: Family Promise of Forsyth County
items.text:
Empowering Families. Strengthening Stability. Transforming Futures.
About
Since 2016, we have been walking alongside families as they build lives filled with stability and hope. Through personalized support, community partnerships, and compassion-driven care, we help families overcome housing instability and move toward lasting independence.
Our Programs
From prevention to empowerment, our programs provide more than just a safety net—they offer a path forward. Families engage with tailored supports like Career Couture, FP on the GO, and THRIVE Workshops to build confidence, skills, and stability.
Resources
This is a go-to space for practical tools, money-saving tips, and community connections. Explore helpful resources that work alongside our programs to support families on their journey toward stability and success.
Get Involved
It takes a community to end family homelessness—and there’s a place for everyone in this work. Whether you volunteer your time, donate, host a drive, or share our mission, your support helps families take real steps toward stability, dignity, and lasting change.

items.title: Appen Media Group
items.text:
Delivering quality news and marketing campaigns to Alpharetta, Roswell, Johns Creek, south Forsyth County, Milton, Dunwoody, Sandy Springs, Decatur and surrounding communities
Appen Media Group (AMG) is a family owned news media company located in the Northern suburbs of Atlanta. The company was founded in 1990 by Ray and Christina Appen, two veteran newspaper executives formerly with Knight-Ridder/The Miami Herald. The company is now led by their son, CEO & Publisher Hans Appen.
Since its inception, AMG has focused on professionally produced local journalism in the areas of government, education, business, public safety, and lifestyle news and features. That core mission remains the same today and AMG’s credible, unbiased, and timely community journalism is now disseminated across a wide spectrum of print, audio and digital platforms.
The AMG product portfolio includes a core of seven weekly community newspapers with a combined home-delivered circulation of 113,000 editions distributed weekly to the affluent metro Atlanta suburbs of Alpharetta, Roswell, Johns Creek, Sandy Springs, Dunwoody, Milton, Decatur and south Forsyth County. AMG provides a competitive advantage in print and digital media in the region in terms of market penetration and community trust. The AMG brand is anchored historically in partnerships within the communities it serves.
AMG has also operated and published news on the award winning appenmedia.com since 1996.
In 2024, AMG purchased the online news hub decaturish.com from longtime owner and founder Dan Whisenhunt. Decaturish serves Decatur and neighboring cities including Avondale Estates, Tucker, Clarkston and Stone Mountain.
In addition to its weekly newspapers and online news websites, AMG assets also include community guides, events, event management, newsletters, custom publications, full service brand development, creative design and production of niche publications.

About Us | Forsyth County School District
Community Outreach
items.text:
Community Outreach
Home
Law Enforcement
The Community Outreach Section consists of the Community Relations, Park Rangers and the Volunteer Unit.
Community Relations Unit
​​​The Community Relations Unit serves to promote safety and education to the citizens and businesses of Forsyth County and is a vital component of the Forsyth County Sheriff’s Office. The FCSO Community Relations Unit is responsible for coordinating and delivering special classes and programs that work to educate the community and to better build the relationship between the community and the Sheriff’s Office. Along with the many courses and programs offered by FCSO Community Relations, they also partner with other organizations throughout the year and attend many other community events.
Classes
Women’s Self Defense
This course is designed to teach women situational awareness by reviewing case studies of previous abductions. Some hands-on training is provided but limited. This class is designed for women and reserved for women only. (Teenagers 14+ can only attend at parent’s discretion due to mature content.)
CRASE
(Citizens Response to Active Shooter Event). Intended to teach what to do/not do in the case of an active shooter. The skills taught are to Avoid, Deny and Defend-STAY ALIVE and Survive!
stranger danger
Educates and empowers children ages 4-11 with knowledge and skills that will help them be safer from various crimes against children.
Programs
Seniors and Lawmen Together
(SALT) Open to all Forsyth County Senior Citizens and held monthly. Each month features different speakers and different topics pertaining to senior safety.
PUBLIC SAFETY CADET PROGRAM
The Public Safety Cadet program is designed to attract young, well-qualified men and women to participate in an organized on the job training program that will prepare them for a career in law enforcement. To learn more, visit the PUBLIC SAFETY CADET PAGE .Neighborhood Watch & Business Watch
Citizens Law Enforcement Academy
(CLEA) The program closely follows the actual hands-on training that deputies undergo. Topics include constitutional law, conducting traffic stops, judgmental use of force, K9 and S.W.A.T. demonstrations, ride alongs with deputies, and much more. Applications are accepted twice a year, watch our Facebook page for those dates. Contact our Community Outreach Section for an application and details.
Neighborhood Watch & Business Watch
This program provides information and specific actions to homeowners that can help protect themselves and their homes. Information covered also includes solutions to common neighborhood problems.
The Business watch program is an offshoot of the Neighborhood Watch concept. The purpose of establishing a Business Watch program is to help educate business proprietors about various precautions they can take in an effort to deter crime. For more information visit the POP page.
